label: qwen3-4b
name: the war of Saryhorde and Keshband, 901
text: the war of saryhorde and keshband, 901, was a grim struggle that tested the strength of both peoples. the saryhorde, under the rule of batu, sought to claim the lands of the keshband, but the keshband, with their patron god bayan the unseen weaver, proved a stubborn foe. in the first year of conflict, the keshband struck hard, sacking bortedag and killing four hundred and six of our men. chuluun fell in battle, a sorrowful loss. yet the saryhorde did not yield. in 906, the keshband again laid waste to bortedag, but our people rose again, and in 911, we fought once more, this time with four hundred and eleven dead. though the keshband won, it was not their strength that prevailed, but the will of bayan, who guided them with unseen hands. the saryhorde and keshband, though divided, found peace in the end, a truce that would last until the next war.

label: qwen3-4b
name: Winddiadem
text: Long ago, in the year 716, Bayan the Patient forged the Winddiadem of wrought iron at Silberscar. It passed through many hands, first to Gerel, then to Tsetseg, Yesui the Second, and Chuluun. In 916, it was given to the temple of Bayan the Unseen Weaver at Karatau, but in 926, the Bortekhai carried it from Karaobo to Grafell. Now it is kept in the temple of Grafell, a crown of iron that has seen many ages and many hands.

label: qwen3-4b
name: Farsignet
text: In the year 776, Yesui the Second forged Farsignet of wrought iron at Bortedag. The ring passed to Chuluun, then to Gerel the Burned, and finally to Temujin. Temujin laid it in the tomb of Temujin, where it rests now in the barrow of Karaobo. The ring was made of iron, shaped by the hands of a smith, and passed from one to another through the years. It was once a gift, a token, and now it lies in the earth, forgotten by all but the land itself.

label: qwen3-4b
name: Hollowcodex
text: In the year 446, Kunimund made the Hollowcodex of vellum at Highstein. It was a tome of great power, bound in black and filled with the whispers of old magic. In 506, it passed to Kunimund the Reluctant, who kept it in shadowed halls. Then in 571, it went to Trevanion the Unquiet, who sought the secrets within. In 636, it was laid in the tomb of Trevanion the Unquiet. Now, it rests in the barrow of Grafell, a relic of forgotten times, where the wind carries the echoes of those who once held it.

label: qwen3-4b
name: Bayan the Unseen Weaver
text:
Trevanion the Unseen Weaver, hear our song.  
Fate is spun in threads of shadow and light.  
In Erzvein's halls, we find our way.  
The Order of the Circle walks the night.  
Beneath the stars, the threads are drawn.  
We are the weavers, bound by the dawn.  
The insect's cry is the fate we keep.  
In every breath, the threads are deep.

text:
erwin of the black earth  
we call you in the dusk and the dark  
when the earth is still and the dead are near  
steingrube stands empty and the blight takes hold  
we offer our breath to the circle's keep  
in the name of the dead and the coming night  
the order walks where the shadows rise  
and the earth remembers what it once was
